questions.q:
Statement: Should plastic carry bags be banned in cities?
Arguments:
I. Yes, they block drains and harm animals that swallow them.
II. No, they are cheap to produce.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.e: The harm to drains and animals is a direct, important reason. Low cost of production does not answer the objection, so it is weak.

questions.q:
Statement: Should every school provide safe drinking water for its students?
Arguments:
I. No, schools already have many other expenses.
II. Yes, clean water is essential for the health of children.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.e: Children's health is a direct and weighty reason for the facility. Other expenses do not outweigh a basic need, so the first argument is weak.

questions.q:
Statement: An advertisement says, "Drink Amrit tea and stay fresh all day."
Assumptions:
I. Some people want to stay fresh through the day.
II. Everyone in the country drinks tea.
o: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit
questions.e: An advertiser assumes that some buyers want the benefit offered. Nothing in the advertisement assumes that everyone drinks tea.

questions.q:
Statement: Many students fell ill after eating food from their school canteen.
Courses of action:
I. The canteen food should be tested and the canteen closed until it is found safe.
II. The school should be shut down for a whole year.
o: Only course of action I follows
Only course of action II follows
Both courses of action I and II follow
Neither course of action I nor II follows
questions.e: Testing the food and pausing the canteen deals directly with the cause. Closing the whole school for a year is an extreme step that does not follow.

questions.q:
Statement: A bridge on a busy road has developed deep cracks.
Courses of action:
I. All roads in the city should be closed to traffic.
II. Heavy vehicles should be stopped from using the bridge until it is repaired.
o: Only course of action I follows
Only course of action II follows
Both courses of action I and II follow
Neither course of action I nor II follows
questions.e: Keeping heavy vehicles off the damaged bridge and repairing it is a sensible step. Closing every road in the city is out of proportion.

questions.q:
Statement: Only members with a library card can borrow books from the college library. Rohit borrowed a book from the college library.
Conclusions:
I. Rohit is a student of the college.
II. Rohit has a library card.
o: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: Borrowing needs a library card, so Rohit must have one. The rule does not say that the members are only students, so the first does not follow.

questions.q:
Statement: "Carry an umbrella today, as the weather office has forecast rain."
Assumptions:
I. The weather office's forecasts are usually reliable.
II. An umbrella gives protection from rain.
o: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit
questions.e: The advice makes sense only if the forecast can be trusted and an umbrella actually keeps one dry. Both are taken for granted.

questions.q:
Statement: Should first-aid training be made compulsory in schools?
Arguments:
I. Yes, it helps students save lives in emergencies.
II. Yes, it builds confidence and a sense of responsibility in students.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.e: Saving lives and building responsibility are both relevant and important benefits, so both arguments are strong.

questions.q:
Statement: The principal told the teachers, "Submit your lesson plans before the term begins so that the syllabus is completed on time."
Assumptions:
I. Planning in advance helps in completing the syllabus on time.
II. No teacher currently prepares any lesson plan.
o: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit
questions.e: The instruction relies on advance planning helping with timely completion. It does not assume that nobody plans at present.

questions.q:
Statement: A notice says, "Install solar water heaters and halve your electricity bill."
Assumptions:
I. Solar water heaters are supplied free to every household.
II. Many people wish to reduce their electricity bills.
o: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit
questions.e: The appeal works only if people want lower bills. Nothing suggests the heaters are free, so the first is not assumed.

questions.q:
Statement: Many accidents occur at night on a stretch of highway because of poor visibility.
Courses of action:
I. Street lights should be installed along that stretch.
II. Police patrolling on the stretch at night should be increased.
o: Only course of action I follows
Only course of action II follows
Both courses of action I and II follow
Neither course of action I nor II follows
questions.e: Better lighting tackles the poor visibility directly, and more night patrolling helps reduce risky driving. Both are sensible and relevant steps.

questions.q:
Statement: Every employee of the firm with at least five years of service is eligible for a loan. Anil is an employee of the firm with seven years of service.
Conclusions:
I. Anil is eligible for a loan.
II. Anil will certainly take a loan.
o: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: Seven years is more than five, so Anil meets the condition and is eligible. Being eligible does not mean he will take the loan.

questions.q:
Statement: Some teachers of the school are members of the sports committee. Every member of the sports committee attended the annual meeting.
Conclusions:
I. Some teachers of the school attended the annual meeting.
II. Every teacher of the school attended the annual meeting.
o: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The teachers who are on the committee attended the meeting, so some teachers attended. Teachers outside the committee may not have attended.

questions.q:
Statement: Should junk food be banned in school canteens?
Arguments:
I. No, because junk food tastes good.
II. Yes, because it harms children's health and ability to concentrate.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.e: Harm to children's health is a strong, direct reason. Taste is a personal preference and does not answer the health concern, so it is weak.

questions.q:
Statement: Should school uniforms be abolished?
Arguments:
I. Yes, because some students do not like the colour of the uniform.
II. Yes, because shops selling casual clothes will earn more.
Which of the following is correct?
o: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.e: Dislike of a colour and the profits of some shops are trivial matters. Neither is a weighty reason to abolish uniforms, so both are weak.

questions.q:
Statements: Every student with full attendance receives a book prize. No suspended student receives a book prize.
Conclusions:
I. No suspended student has full attendance.
II. Every student who receives a book prize has full attendance.
o: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: A suspended student with full attendance would receive a prize, which contradicts the second statement. The second conclusion reverses the first statement, which is not allowed.

questions.q:
Statements: Only graduates can apply for the post of clerk. Sunil is not a graduate.
Conclusions:
I. Sunil has not applied for the post of clerk.
II. Sunil is not eligible to apply for the post of clerk.
o: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The rule is about eligibility, so a non-graduate like Sunil is not eligible. It does not tell us whether he actually applied, so conclusion I does not follow.

questions.q:
Statement: "The new pest-resistant seed raises crop yield, so the government should give it free to small farmers."
Assumptions:
I. Small farmers may not be able to buy the seed on their own.
II. The pest-resistant seed damages the soil.
o: Only assumption I is implicit
Only assumption II is implicit
Both assumptions I and II are implicit
Neither assumption I nor II is implicit
questions.e: Free distribution is suggested because small farmers might otherwise not afford the seed. A claim that the seed damages the soil would work against the proposal.

questions.q:
Statement: A study found that students who sleep at least eight hours score higher marks in tests on average.
Conclusions:
I. Every student who sleeps eight hours scores high marks.
II. A student who sleeps less than eight hours can never score high marks.
o: Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.e: The finding speaks only about averages. It does not guarantee high marks for each such student, nor rule out high marks for those who sleep less.

questions.q:
Statement: Heavy rain has pushed a river above the danger mark and villages on its bank may be flooded.
Courses of action:
I. People living in the low-lying villages should be shifted to safe shelters.
II. Relief camps with food and medical aid should be set up for the shifted people.
o: Only course of action I follows
Only course of action II follows
Both courses of action I and II follow
Neither course of action I nor II follows
questions.e: Moving people to safety protects them from the flood, and relief camps look after those who are moved. Both steps are practical and follow from the situation.
